claims.text: An active-learning machine-learning interatomic potential trained iteratively on short AIMD trajectories can compute solid and liquid free energies near fusion.
The proposed ML workflow can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling in the calculated free energies.
The proposed workflow will substantially reduce computational cost relative to explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
Short AIMD trajectories will be generated separately for solid and liquid configurations.
Active learning can cover the configuration space needed to represent the entire relevant potential-energy surface.
Iterative improvement of the ML potential will make it accurately reproduce solid–liquid free-energy differences.
Thermodynamic integration or another enhanced-sampling method will be run using the ML potential.
The ML potential mediates the method by representing interatomic interactions and the free-energy landscape.
Active learning preferentially improves accuracy in regions of configuration space that are critical for free-energy evaluation.
Replacing most explicit AIMD sampling with ML-potential sampling preserves the essential entropy and anharmonic contributions while reducing cost.
The method will predict phase free-energy curves, melting temperatures, and latent heats within approximately 5% of explicit AIMD results.
The method will be 10–100 times faster than both traditional AIMD and TOR-TILD.
Explicit AIMD free-energy evaluation is highly accurate but computationally intensive.
Computational treatment becomes especially difficult for multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The workflow is intended to progress from elemental and binary validation systems to high-entropy alloys containing up to five principal elements.
The intended temperature range is approximately 1000–3000 K near melting transitions.
Prior applications of ML potentials to elemental and binary systems provide promising preliminary evidence for the proposed fusion workflow.
It is uncertain whether the ML model can capture electron–vibration coupling, strong anharmonicity, and rare configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys without extensive retraining.
A decisive benchmark will compare the proposed method against full AIMD and TOR-TILD for both phase free-energy curves, melting temperature, and latent heat.
The hypothesis is falsified if errors relative to full AIMD exceed 5% or if systematic failures occur in the entropy contributions associated with anharmonicity or electron–vibration coupling.
